item.title: [ZEPPELIN-183] Different Notebooks are Sharing the Same Context
item.description: Currently notebooks are sharing the same context: a table loaded and registered in a notebook can be accessed from another notebook.
item.summary: Different Notebooks are Sharing the Same Context

status.description: A resolution has been taken, and it is awaiting verification by reporter. From here issues are either reopened, or are closed.

comments.comment:
+10 on this JIRA.

The sharing of context and variables among all notebooks for a given interpreter is a real issue right now. Not only it breaks completely user context isolation but also it can introduce subtle bugs very hard to debug, not even mentioning multi-tenant usage.

The only work-around right now is to create different instances for a given interpreter if you wish to isolate the scope of your notebook.

But I guess having the Context scope to the notebook level might be a right level.

Still, it raises many concerns about tech implementation. For example, the Spark interpreter relies on the SparkREPL. Is it relevant to have 1 instance of the REPL per notebook, resource-wise ?

This causes problems with the dependency loader too, because dependencies may only be added before the spark context is used. Another note may have been used already, thus loading the context and blocking any opportunity to add a dependency.

Keep in mind that only a single SparkContext may be used in a given JVM (SPARK-2243).

Sharing the same context has proven to be an issue... and makes it really hard from the multi-tenant perspective as you need to make sure everything has a unique name across all notebooks, even the ones from other users...

        Try to use both notebook with the same interpreter setting.

Github user vijikarthi commented on the pull request:

@Leemoonsoo The latest commits seems to be working. I could see two different SC getting created in "isolated" mode. However when the second SparkContext is getting created, I am hitting an exception which is related to "SPARK-10872"

Regarding proxy user support, I am not sure if we can handle it inside "SparkInterpreter". The way spark-submit handles proxy-user is by running the main process itself as the proxy user (see https://github.com/apache/spark/blob/master/core/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/deploy/SparkSubmit.scala#L160). In our case if we run the "RemoteInterpreterServer" as the proxy user, the rest of the flow is kind of taken care automatically. I have tested with/without Kerberos (by adding SPARK_SUBMIT_OPTIONS="--proxy-user vijay -v" in bin/zeppelin-env.sh) and it works fine.

Github user Leemoonsoo commented on the pull request:

https://github.com/apache/incubator-zeppelin/pull/795#issuecomment-214979591

@vijikarthi Thanks for testing. 'SPARK-10872' is expected while default configuration of sparkcontext creates 'metastore_db' in the same location. If you configure hive-site.xml to use mysql or something else for it's metastore, the errors will gone. Alternatively, you can set 'zeppelin.spark.useHiveContext' to 'false' in Interpreter menu, if you're not relying on HiveQL.

Regarding proxy user support, If passing "--proxy-user" argument in SPARK_SUBMIT_OPTIONS is the only way, Zeppelin needs extra mechanism to pass this argument. Thanks for sharing the details and user test result!
